We're looking for a hands-on Operations Manager to own the operational and analytical supply side of our GPU fleet. Key focus areas: GPU fleet lifecycle, health, observability, utilization monitoring, and remediation across our neocloud and bare metal environments.
We contract for a fixed amount of compute capacity. GPUs drift from healthy to unhealthy over time, and this role minimizes that downtime to keep the maximum number of GPUs healthy at any given moment.
This is an operator role, not people management. You'll drive execution through clear processes, metrics, reporting, vendor coordination, and cross-functional alignment..

Drive suppliers to keep the maximum amount of the GPU fleet online and healthy.
Maintain a live reconciliation of contracted vs. provisioned vs. healthy vs. utilized capacity, broken out by supplier and by cluster maximizing the number of healthy GPUs.
Supplier-attributed fleet health accountability: own replacement SLAs, mean time to repair (MTTR), and RMA cycle times for every in-scope supplier.
SLA monitoring, credit claims, and remedy enforcement: track SLA performance against contract terms, file and pursue credit claims, and drive remediation plans when suppliers fall short.
Drive internal communications where suppliers need to perform maintenance to ensure all Baseten stakeholders are aware of activities that impact availability.
Scope and Approach
Flexibility: this list covers the core of the role, not the limit of it. You'll be asked to take on adjacent work as the function evolves and as new gaps surface.
Ownership mindset: we need someone who treats "whatever it takes" as a genuine operating principle, not a line in a job posting. If something falls outside a defined lane but inside the overall goal of closing the capacity gap, it's yours to pick up.

5 to 10+ years within infrastructure working within the compute lifecycle to maximize functional compute, ideally in a hyperscale, cloud, or large-scale compute environment.
Direct experience managing GPU, server, or data center hardware supplier relationships. You understand fleet health, RMA processes, and how contracted capacity differs from delivered capacity.
Highly analytical. You should be comfortable pulling your own data, building your own reports, and generating insights without waiting on someone else to hand you a dashboard.
Comfortable with ambiguity. Part of the job is figuring out what should exist and building it.
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills. You'll work closely with finance, infrastructure/engineering, legal, and security on a regular basis.

Experience at a hyperscaler, neo cloud provider, or AI infrastructure company
Familiarity with GPU hardware lifecycles (NVIDIA H100/H200/GB200 class systems), power/thermal constraints, and supply chain dynamics for compute.
Experience running formal supplier corrective actions.

AI-fluent. You already use AI tools in your day-to-day work to analyze information, automate repetitive tasks, draft materials, and work more efficiently.

This role is pivotal in evaluating the mission effectiveness, survivability, and operational impact of our autonomy solutions across multiple platforms and domains. You will work closely with engineering, product development, and defense stakeholders to inform design trade-offs, assess system performance, and optimize mission capabilities.
This position requires a deep understanding of military operations, wargaming, modeling & simulation (M&S), analytic techniques, and operational analysis techniques. Your work will directly shape Shield AI’s strategy by identifying how our AI-powered platforms can best serve the evolving needs of modern warfare.

Develop and execute operational analysis strategies to assess the effectiveness of autonomous aircraft in real-world military scenarios.
Lead modeling, simulation, and wargaming efforts to evaluate system performance, mission impact, and survivability in contested environments.
Work closely with engineering teams and product managers to translate operational insights into design decisions and system improvements.
Conduct trade studies and sensitivity analyses to assess system performance under varying operational conditions and threats.
Utilize advanced modeling & simulation tools (e.g., AFSIM, STK, MATLAB, Python) to develop high-fidelity mission models.
Analyze force-on-force engagements, sensor effectiveness, and autonomy-driven decision-making to optimize mission success.
Collaborate with DoD stakeholders, operators, and warfighters to understand mission needs and align system capabilities with operational requirements.
Support concept of operations (CONOPS) development for new AI-driven aircraft capabilities.
Identify emerging threats and operational challenges, ensuring Shield AI’s systems remain ahead of adversary capabilities.
Develop and present technical reports, briefings, and recommendations to senior leadership, customers, and government agencies.
Leverage modern compute and development best practices (e.g., scalable cloud/HPC workflows, containerization, version control, CI/CD, and automated testing) to build, run, and iterate high-fidelity simulation and analysis pipelines quickly and reliably.

5+ years of experience in operational analysis, modeling & simulation (M&S), or military operations research.
Expertise in military mission analysis, operational planning, and wargaming methodologies.
Proficiency with AFSIM, STK, MATLAB, or other M&S tools used for aerospace and defense applications.
Deep understanding of air combat, ISR, electronic warfare, or autonomous systems in contested environments.
Experience working with DoD stakeholders, warfighters, and government agencies to align capabilities with mission requirements.
Demonstrated ability to seamlessly apply modern compute, data science, and software development best practices (e.g., cloud/HPC workflows, containerization, Git-based version control, CI/CD, automated testing, and reproducible analysis) to build and maintain reliable simulations and analytics.
Excellent communication and briefing skills, with experience presenting to senior leadership, customers, and military personnel.
Ability to work in a fast-paced, agile development environment with shifting priorities.

Prior experience in force-on-force analysis, CONOPS development, or military campaign modeling.
Familiarity with DoD acquisition processes, Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS), and military operational testing.
Experience integrating AI-driven decision-making algorithms into operational analysis frameworks.
Prior military service or experience working with U.S. Air Force, Navy, or Special Operations Forces.
Experience using GenAI to structure problems and create simulation or analysis tools.
Active Secret or Top-Secret clearance (or ability to obtain one).

About Betterment
Betterment is a leading, technology-driven financial services company that offers investing, savings and retirement solutions for retail investors and investment advisors as well as financial wellness solutions, including a 401(k) for small and medium-sized businesses.

Our team is passionate about our mission, to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease. We’re headquartered in NYC and offer hybrid NY-based positions (four days/ week in-office, with no required office days during the summer and winter holidays).

We're hiring an analyst and builder for our Revenue Operations team to be a force multiplier for our go-to-market organization. Sometimes that means tackling a question with no playbook yet. Sometimes it means running an established process and improving it as you go.
You'll take on ambiguous, high impact questions and turn them into clearly defined problems, design the right solution, and drive it through build, adoption, and continuous improvement.
The role has three modes. First, you'll drive the analytical core: forecasting, executive reporting, revenue planning, QBR-grade analyses over large datasets, quota and target analytics, and the models that support forecasting and planning. You'll present your own work directly to leadership and translate complex business questions into actionable insights.
Second, you'll build net-new systems: internal tools, data models, and reporting infrastructure that teammates then run and scale. That includes planning models, dashboards, and operational workflows that make the business more efficient over time.
Third, you'll make Revenue Operations more leveraged with AI, whether that's building AI-assisted tooling, designing account scoring and research logic in our go-to-market stack, or automating work that shouldn't be manual. You’ll constantly look for more opportunities to increase leverage across the organization.
The ideal candidate combines strong analytical horsepower with a systems mindset and genuine comfort with ambiguity. You ask why until you understand the business objective behind a request, you design solutions that scale beyond the first use case, and you already use AI to build and move faster than your job title suggests.

You’re naturally curious about how AI can improve the way work gets done, but you know technology is only valuable when it solves a real business problem. And you finish: to you, work is done when it's adopted, documented, and running without you, not when the analysis is shipped.
This role is based out of our NYC office.

About Motorway
Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships.

Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.
This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

We're now applying that same model to Enterprise: the part of the market where businesses, not private individuals, sell vehicles to dealers. It's 2 million of the 8 million used cars sold in the UK each year, a quarter of the total market.
In May 2026 we launched our Enterprise remarketing service with Mobilize Financial Services (the finance arm behind Renault, Nissan, Dacia and Alpine) as our first customer (see launch article here ).

Mobilize’s end-of-lease customers profile their car through Motorway’s market-leading app, we auction the vehicle directly to dealers, and the vehicle is collected from the customer at the end of the lease.

This cuts weeks out of a process that used to require physical storage sites and repeat transport, saving costs and time; and delivering a better customer experience.
This role joins the Enterprise team that is building this business line from the ground up. It's a rare chance to shape a new, fast-growing product inside an already fast-growing scale-up, and help rebuild a part of the automotive industry that our CEO has called "well overdue a rebuild." If you’re excited about building a ground-breaking business that redefines an industry, this role is for you.

The Enterprise Operations Team sits at the centre of this new, high-growth business line. You'll be the main point of contact for our enterprise lease customers, guiding them through every step of the return and inspection process, and you'll work directly with purchasing dealer partners to keep the buying process smooth on their side too.
Every interaction you handle shapes how supported, informed and confident our lease customers and dealers feel. The structured approach and attention to detail you bring drives operational excellence and keeps customer satisfaction high as we grow in the lease vehicle market.
You'll be joining an ambitious new chapter for Motorway from day one.

This is a generalist role where you will be working with customers and dealers managing the end-to-end sales process from the initial vehicle appraisal through to final inspection and collection:
Enterprise Customer Contact: Be the primary point of contact for enterprise lease customers via phone (inbound and outbound) email and WhatsApp, guiding them through their vehicle return and inspection process.
Customer Calls: Conduct customer calls to verify identity, review vehicle inspections, confirm eligibility, and set clear expectations around next steps.
Manage Vehicle Profiling: Gather and validate vehicle details including mileage, service history, condition and inspection photos to prepare vehicles for sale.
Set Expectations Clearly: Explain inspection outcomes, indicative charges, collection process in a clear, concise and professional manner.
Coordinate Collections: Capture preferred collection dates, confirm logistics and ensure all transport details are accurately recorded.
Process Vehicles End to End: Move vehicles through each operational stage from onboarding and enquiry creation to sale readiness, post sale support and invoice creation ensuring accurate handover.
Handle Post Sale Queries: Generate and share damage reports, support customer questions and assist with post sale updates.
Maintain Operational Accuracy: Keep systems, trackers and dashboards fully up to date to meet quality, compliance and SLA standards.
Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Collaborate closely with Transport, B2B Sales Specialist and Strategic Account teams to ensure a smooth, joined up customer experience.
Achieve Performance Targets: Work towards quality, productivity and customer experience targets while following defined enterprise processes.

Betriebsleiter\*in Baubetrieb (100%)
====================================
Unser Ziel ist es, Jugendlichen Fähigkeiten zu vermitteln, damit sie ihren Weg im Leben selbstständig gehen können. Dafür arbeiten bei uns Sozialpädagogik, Schule, Therapie und Berufsbildung eng zusammen. In unseren Betrieben lernen Jugendliche einen Beruf – begleitet von Fachpersonen, die nicht nur ihr Handwerk verstehen, sondern auch Menschen.
Du bist eine coole Socke, hast etwas auf dem Kasten und möchtest dein Handwerk mit echter Verantwortung verbinden? Wir suchen **so rasch wie möglich** zur Ergänzung unseres Baubetriebs in Hausen am Albis ein\*e
**Betriebsleiter\*in Baubetrieb (100%)**
----------------------------------------
**Das begeistert dich**
* Du hältst die Fäden zusammen: Du organisierst unseren Baubetrieb mit 3–4 Mitarbeitenden und rund 5 Lernenden, planst Aufträge und Einsätze und sorgst dafür, dass alle wissen, was wann zu tun ist
* Du bist vom Fach und packst an: Ob \-, Gipser\-, Umbau\- oder Renovationsarbeiten – du bist mittendrin statt nur dabei
* Du führst mit Kopf und Herz: Du hast dein Team im Griff, kannst Verantwortung abgeben und findest auch im manchmal etwas turbulenten Alltag mit Jugendlichen den richtigen Ton
* Du machst Handwerker von morgen: Du begleitest unsere Lernenden fachlich und persönlich, bereitest sie auf das QV vor und übernimmst den Berufsfachschulunterricht im Rahmen unserer Ausbildung
* Du hast ein gutes Händchen für Kundschaft: Du trittst professionell auf, findest Lösungen und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Aufträge sauber, zuverlässig und zur Zufriedenheit unserer Kundschaft erledigt werden
* Du willst nicht einfach verwalten: Du bringst Ideen ein, entwickelst den Betrieb weiter und machst Albisbrunn als Ausbildungsort jeden Tag ein Stück besser
**Das bringst du mit**
* Du hast eine Ausbildung im Bauhandwerk, idealerweise als Polier, und bringst mehrere Jahre Berufserfahrung im Baugewerbe mit
* Führungserfahrung, Organisationstalent und unternehmerisches Denken gehören zu deinen Stärken
* Kosten, Budgets, Termine und Qualität hast du im Griff und arbeitest selbstständig und zuverlässig
* Du bist Berufsbildner oder hast Lust, diese Ausbildung zu machen, und gibst dein Fachwissen gerne verständlich und mit Freude weiter
* Du bist offen, teamfähig und wertschätzend und hast Lust, Jugendliche mit unterschiedlichen Stärken, Herausforderungen und Entwicklungstempi zu begleiten
* Du sprichst und verstehst Schweizerdeutsch und kannst dich adressatengerecht, klar und unkompliziert mit Jugendlichen, Mitarbeitenden und Kundschaft verständigen
**Das erwartet dich**
* ein traumhaft schöner Arbeitsort
* ein aufgestelltes Team, vielleicht das beste der Welt
* flache Hierarchien
* mind. 5 Wochen Ferien
* ein nicht alltägliches, interessantes Umfeld eines Jugendheims
* Personalrestaurant, private Benutzung von Fitnessraum, Schwimmteich, Sporthalle mit Kletterwand uvm.

Alan therapy: members can book a therapy session with psychologists. You maintain smooth relationships with our psychologists, ensure therapy demand matches the supply and contribute to several steps of their lifecycle at Alan (hiring, onboarding, invoicing, supporting booking management etc).
Claims: We provide a best-in-class claims experience, including our own optic care service. You treat claims and assist in decisions regarding our coverage. About Substrate
Substrate is the critical infrastructure layer between AI and biology. AI for biology has a data problem, not a compute problem: biological foundation models can predict but cannot experiment, and the large-scale, high-quality data they need does not exist. We are building the lab that generates it, with quality and provenance built in. We are not a CRO and we are not a cloud lab.
The company was founded by Mostafa ElSayed, co-founder and CEO; Oli Hoy, who leads the lab buildout and operations; Alexey Morgunov, who leads science and intelligence software; and Anna Huyghues-Despointes, who leads partnerships and go-to-market.

You will run the day-to-day operations of our lab in London, and be the person the scientists come to when something is missing, broken, late or lost. The day-one work is what you would expect: consumables and stock, goods in and cold chain, equipment servicing and calibration, suppliers and purchasing, waste streams and safety records.
Three parts go beyond a standard lab operations job. The first is provenance. Every experiment we sell carries a record of what went into it, down to the lot of the consumable used and the conditions material was held in. If a lot number is not captured, the data point is worth less, and that record runs through you.
The second is that the systems are not written yet. Inventory, goods in, asset registers and ordering exist in no form that will survive the next year. You define what the lab has to capture and work with the science and software teams to make sure it does.
The third is that sample handling and stock control here get automated, and you help specify the system that does it. Every sample, plate, reagent and consumable lot carries a barcode, scanned at each point it is handled, so the record is created by the work rather than reconstructed afterwards.

The same scan draws stock down, which turns reordering from a weekly count into something the system flags before anyone is short. Our software team is building that layer now and the requirements have to come from the lab floor: what gets a barcode, where the scan points sit, and what happens when a label will not read.

Some find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing which one you are.
Your first 90 days
First 30 days
Take ownership of goods in: every delivery received, booked in, stored correctly and recorded.
Map how material moves through the lab and build the first accurate picture of what we hold. That map is the input to a fully barcoded scheme and system.
Days 30 to 60
Put a working inventory and reorder system in place, with minimum levels set from real consumption rather than guesses, and own the purchasing loop.
Agree the barcode and labelling scheme with the software team, and get equipment records in one place.
Days 60 to 90
Run the lab as a routine that does not depend on being asked, with the barcoded system live across one workflow, goods-in to bench to stock draw-down, feeding our provenance record.

You have run the physical side of a lab where being out of stock stops the work: biotech, pharma, a university or institute lab, or a manufacturing or diagnostics operation built around one.

Lab consumables and the rhythm of a working lab are already familiar to you, you have handled real volume and real inventory, and you know the difference between a system that works on paper and one that works at eight on a Monday morning.

We are not asking for a particular speciality, but you should arrive able to run the lab rather than learn what one needs.

Two or more years running a lab or comparable physical operation, hands-on and accountable for the result.
Practical stock control: goods in, inventory records, reorder points, stock counts that reconcile.
Buying from suppliers: raising orders, comparing quotes, managing lead times.
Hands-on with a barcoded or scanned stock system, including what goes wrong when people skip the scan.
Lab environment experience: cold storage, hazardous waste, containment, controlled materials.

Health and safety training such as IOSH.
Developed or co-developed a barcode system for autonomous workflows in labs, including working with software development teams to implement it.
How we work and who you will work with
This role is on site five days a week at 20 Triton Street in London, because the lab is a physical place and the work is in it. The wider founding team is distributed across London, New York and Europe.

You will report to Simon Varzandeh, a member of our scientific staff working on protein characterisation and one of the lab's heaviest users, and work alongside the protein science and functional genomics teams, the engineers building the tracking and stock system with you, and operations on facilities, health and safety and purchasing.

You will be the first person here whose whole job is focused on the lab floor.
We work in the open and each person owns their area. UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover.

Spreedly is the world's leading Open Payments Platform. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, the company gives mid-market and enterprise businesses the infrastructure to connect to any payment gateway, processor, or fraud tool through a single API. The platform is vendor-agnostic by design, meaning customers are never locked into a single provider and never need to rebuild their payments stack to access new capabilities.
The core business problem Spreedly solves is real and costly: global merchants face a fragmented payments ecosystem, where every new market, payment method, or fraud tool typically requires a separate, time-consuming integration. Spreedly eliminates that complexity, enabling companies to route transactions intelligently, secure cardholder data, prevent fraud, and expand into new markets without heavy engineering overhead.

Spreedly is building a new go-to-market operations function, and we're hiring a Lead Revenue Operations Analyst to help run it. Revenue Operations is joining Business Operations, and rather than migrate the function as-is, we're pivoting it into a broader GTM Operations pillar — one built to run a predictable, efficient go-to-market operating engine.
This is a senior individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities, reporting to the Sr. Director of Business Operations and serving as a trusted thought partner to our SVP of Revenue.

You will own sales forecasting, pipeline and performance analytics, GTM planning, and sales compensation strategy, combining quantitative analysis and qualitative analysis with broader business context to inform decisions.

You will go beyond reporting what happened. You will independently identify what is changing in the business, understand why, and translate complex data into clear insights and recommendations that help Revenue leadership act early — for example, spotting churn risk in the funnel before it becomes lost revenue.

This role is designed for someone who wants significant impact through expertise, judgment, analytical rigor, and execution rather than through managing a team. You will operate with significant autonomy, partnering directly with executive and sales leadership to turn analysis into action.

Own the sales forecasting process end-to-end — methodology, pipeline inspection, risk identification, and forecast accuracy — and run the cadence that gives leadership clear, actionable views of existing and new-customer opportunities

Own revenue operations planning and partner with Revenue and Finance leadership on GTM planning, including quotas, capacity, headcount, targets, and scenario planning
Own sales compensation strategy, design, and governance, including quota and incentive modeling, performance analysis, and oversight of commission accuracy, while partnering with the GTM Operations Analyst on day-to-day plan administration and commission processing.
Partner with sales, marketing, and executive leaders on go-to-market decisions, including revenue-operations considerations for tools and processes such as CPQ and deal desk

About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
RevOps at Wayflyer is a team of builders. We're not just looking for people who can spot what's broken and flag it, that skill matters and we have great people who do it well. We're looking for people who also have the technical range to build the fix themselves, independently, without waiting on someone else's roadmap.
We sit at the epicenter of an exceptionally fast-growing business running across multiple channels and partners, and it's our job to make sure the systems underneath that growth have the ability to scale. This role is for a builder who wants to see the impact of their work fast, ideally in seconds, while still thinking several steps ahead so today's quick fix doesn't turn into next year's technical debt. We want people who enjoy the instant feedback loop just as much as the long game.
What you'll actually do
Integrations & Technical Ownership: Build, maintain and improve the systems, internal automations and integrations that make our sales and CS teams faster and more effective, from the ground up.
AI-Native Systems: Build, deploy and continuously sharpen AI-native workflows and agents that augment how Sales, CS and the wider Revenue org work, not just automate around the edges.
Data, Analytics & Problem Solving: Use self-sourced data to diagnose what's actually broken, run root cause analysis, and build the fix yourself, then measure it against real KPIs and keep iterating.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Project Ownership: Work directly with Sales, Partnerships, Marketing and Finance to turn half-formed requirements into systems that actually solve the problem.
Revenue Data Hygiene: Own regular audits, deduplication, enrichment and the process fixes that keep our data usable across every system that touches it.
Driving Operational Excellence: Spot inefficiencies before anyone asks you to, prioritise ruthlessly, and build the automated solutions that let the function scale without adding headcount.
What this role could turn into
This function sits at the intersection of Revenue, Marketing, Finance, Data and Engineering, so you'll get exposure most people spend years angling for. People who do this well tend to move toward GTM strategy, GTM engineering, product roles, and beyond. The sky is the limit.
Who thrives here
You're an AI-native builder who thinks in scale, not one-off fixes, and gets uncomfortable when you spot a manual workaround. You're just as comfortable pairing with Engineering as you are in the room with Sales leadership, translating one for the other without losing anything in the middle.

You run towards the hardest, messiest problems, you don't wait for permission, and you don't need a fully-scoped brief before you start. You're always watching what the best GTM teams are building, and you'd rather pitch a bold idea than ship another incremental tweak.
We hire for range
3+ years in RevOps, MarOps, consulting or similar, but tenure isn't the point, trajectory is. Whatever your background, you're an AI-native builder with strong business acumen and a sharp eye for the difference between a good customer experience and a bad one.
You bring fluency in Python (or Node) and SQL, hands-on experience configuring HubSpot and its developer suite, and comfort with automation platforms like Zapier, Pipedream, n8n or UiPath.

You've likely configured CPQ, CLM, sales engagement or customer-success platforms before, and just as importantly, you've driven adoption of something you built, not just shipped it and walked away. Extra credit if you've built and deployed AI agents, integrated AI/LLM-based solutions into existing workflows, or built automated pipelines end to end.
Location and working policy
📍 Dublin or London, Hybrid
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and pension. Equity, because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

Payments at Gusto aren't just infrastructure, they're the reason people get paid on time, every time. Payment Operations sits within Gusto's Money team, a cross-functional group spanning Engineering, Product, and Operations that powers money movement across Gusto's growing product surface: core payroll, contractor payments, international money movement, and new business offerings like PEO.
As the Payment Operations Manager, you'll lead a team of Payment Operations Analysts and own the health of Gusto's payment operations end to end: the ACH, wire, RTP, and international contractor payment rails, the day-to-day operations behind our bank and payment partner relationships, and the operational side of the compliance programs that keep all of it running within regulatory bounds. You'll work closely with Engineering, Product, Accounting, Risk, Legal, and CX to get there.
This is a role for someone who can zoom in and personally work a ticket or partner escalation, and zoom out to manage the team and keep a compliance program on track, in the same afternoon. You build strong people, hold partners accountable, and bring rigor to how the team operates.

Manage a team of Payment Operations Analysts. Hire, coach, and develop them, set clear expectations, and give direct feedback. Own team-level SLAs, on-call rotation and escalation paths, and reporting, and use data to spot where the team's processes are breaking down and fix the root cause, not just the symptom. You're accountable for the team's output and for the growth of the people on it.
Manage day-to-day bank and payment partner operations
Own the operational relationship with our banking and payment partners, including issue triage, escalations, and operational reviews, and personally work individual tickets yourself when the queue backs up or SLAs are at risk. Partner closely with the team that owns the strategic partnership on renewals and due diligence.
Operate the compliance programs that keep payments running
Execute the day-to-day work behind Gusto's Nacha, unclaimed property, and bank compliance programs, and Payment Ops' portion of SOC 1 audits. Financial Services Compliance and Payroll Compliance own these programs; you're the operational partner who keeps documentation, controls, and evidence current and coordinates with them and GRC when new requirements land.
Drive incident response for payment operations
When something breaks at scale, whether it's a failed batch, a reconciliation break, or a payment partner outage, you're in the investigation yourself, not just directing it. You keep stakeholders informed and drive the retro that prevents it from happening again.
Partner with Product and Engineering
Bring the team's operational insight into product and engineering conversations. Flag risk early, weigh in on payment-related specs, and make sure operational needs are represented, without owning the product roadmap yourself.
Lead with AI
Model and encourage the use of AI across the team, whether that's faster investigation, cleaner documentation, or automating repetitive work.

We are looking for a Chief of Staff–style operator to serve as the President’s right hand and help run, maintain, and continuously evolve the Product, Engineering & Design operating model and cadence.
This role will turn strategy into a durable execution system. You will own the connective tissue across the President’s leadership cadence: preparing the right inputs, creating clarity on decisions and tradeoffs, ensuring commitments are followed through, surfacing risks early, and improving the operating model as the organization changes.

You will work across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Finance, People, and your peers in Business Operations, partnering with senior leaders who do not report to you and influencing through judgment, trust, and clarity.
The successful candidate will combine executive judgment, operational rigor, business acumen, comfort with ambiguity, strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to move fluidly between strategic questions and the execution details required to make the system work.
AI fluency is an important part of this role. You will use approved enterprise AI tools, including tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable platforms, to automate repeatable operating work, synthesize information across functions, improve leadership preparation, surface risks and dependencies, and accelerate strategic-initiative delivery.
This role reports to the VP of Operations at Squarespace and is based remotely in California or locally at our New York City headquarters.
You’ll Get To…
Run the President's operating cadence . Own end-to-end orchestration of the leadership rhythm: staff meetings, WBRs, MBRs, and QBRs, finance and portfolio reviews, priority updates, and annual operating-plan inputs. Ensure each ritual has a clear purpose, owner, input, output, decision authority, and downstream cascade.
Drive decision quality. Synthesize diverse inputs into concise narratives that make priorities, risks, options, tradeoffs, and recommended decisions clear to the President and leadership team. Document decisions in the room, assign owners and deadlines, track commitments, and escalate unresolved issues with context and a proposed path forward.
Improve execution velocity. Identify alignment and execution risks before they surface as leadership surprises, and facilitate resolution across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Customer Operations, Finance, People, and Business Operations, connecting planning, performance, financial, organizational, and roadmap inputs. Use AI and advanced tooling to make decisions faster and better-informed.
Evolve the operating model. Treat the operating system as a living thing. Establish health measures such as decision latency, action closure, cascade reach, pre-read quality, participation, recurring issue themes, and use them to assess whether rituals, artifacts, and escalation paths are producing the right outcomes.

Recommend and implement changes to cadence, governance, templates, roles, and channels as strategy and priorities evolve, codifying what works so the model is easy for leaders to understand and operate.
Lead high-priority strategic initiatives. Drive complex, ambiguous, cross-functional work on behalf of the President, from framing and workplan through decision, implementation, and follow-through, including emerging problems that don't yet have a clear owner. Support annual strategy, goals, headcount, and budget processes by connecting them to the department's operating rhythm.
Represent the President and build transparency. Stand in for the President in meetings, events, and discussions, exercising the remit of the position. Navigate difficult conversations and cross-functional tradeoffs without relying on formal authority. Support two-way access to the President through Town Halls, Roundtables, Office Hours, and written follow-up, using sound judgment about what should be broadly communicated, selectively shared, or handled privately.
Serve as a trusted thought partner to the President and senior leadership team, offering an independent perspective and respectfully challenging assumptions when needed.

Significant experience in Chief of Staff, Product Operations, Business Operations, Strategy & Operations, or management consulting
A track record of owning an operating model, leadership cadence, or portfolio of complex cross-functional initiatives, preferably in tech companies
Knowledge of the product / software development lifecycle
Demonstrated proficiency with enterprise AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable approved tools, and experience integrating them into daily workflows to automate repeatable tasks, optimize processes, improve synthesis, and accelerate project delivery.
Exceptional written communication: you can turn a large volume of input into a concise, decision-ready narrative tailored to the audience
Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand metrics, forecasts, resource tradeoffs, product or portfolio performance, and organizational implications.
Strong executive presence and facilitation skills; you can create clarity and momentum in high-stakes or ambiguous settings.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, build consensus, resolve conflict, and push for decisions without formal authority.
High judgment and discretion when handling sensitive organizational, people, financial, and strategic information.
Comfort operating in ambiguity, switching between strategic altitude and detailed execution, and taking ownership of problems that cross organizational boundaries.
A continuous-improvement mindset: you distinguish between process and content, challenge ineffective routines, and make change practical and durable.
A bias toward action, paired with the judgment to know when to decide, when to seek input, and when to escalate.
What Success Looks Like

s.h: In the first 6–12 months, you will
s.t:
Implement a dependable operating rhythm in which leadership forums are well-prepared, decision-oriented, and followed through.
Improve the quality and consistency of pre-reads, decision logs, action tracking, portfolio updates, and quarterly communications.
Make it easy to see what changed, what matters now, what decisions are needed, who owns the next step, and where risk is accumulating.
Establish a small number of reliable AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual preparation and reporting effort, improve the timeliness and quality of leadership inputs, and make follow-through more visible.
Increase the organization’s ability to reuse knowledge, detect recurring issues, and move from raw information to clear decisions without adding unnecessary process.
Build strong working relationships and trust with the President and his leaders across the department and company, leading with tact, discretion and respect.
Help the President and leadership team make faster, clearer, better-informed decisions without adding unnecessary processes or meetings.
Leave the system more scalable and more resilient than you found it.

The Senior Operations Manager helps ensure the account operates efficiently and has the processes, information, and coordination needed to support successful delivery.

Reporting to the Director of Operations and Project Management, this role supports a broad range of operational needs, including systems and processes, resourcing, workflows, access management, partner coordination, and other activities that support the account’s day-to-day operations.

The Operations Manager works across internal teams and external partners to keep information accurate, drive timely follow-through, and identify and escalate operational risks.

Operational systems and process management
Day-to-day administration of the systems, tools, trackers, and documentation used to operate the account.
Implementation and maintenance of operational processes, SOPs, R&Rs, intake processes, escalation paths, and ways-of-working documentation.
Monitoring adoption and identifying recurring workflow issues, inefficiencies, or gaps for escalation to the Director of Operations and Project Management.
Coordination of operational readiness for new systems, tools, and process rollouts.
Resourcing and capacity management
Maintenance of allocation, availability, open-role, freelance, transition, leave, and capacity tracking across the business.
Coordination with Account, Project Management, Casting, and department leads to keep resourcing information current.
Preparation of recurring capacity and resourcing reporting for Operations and account leadership.
Identification and escalation of allocation issues, coverage gaps, and staff-plan discrepancies.
Administrative coordination of approved staffing changes, while Project Management retains ownership of project-level assignments and delivery needs.
Finance and procurement operations
Maintenance of operational inputs and audit trails for scope, budget, burn, reconciliation, invoices, purchase orders, vendors, and payments.
Coordination with Finance, Account, Project Management, and Production to ensure financial information is accurate and submitted on time.
Monitoring and follow-up on invoices, job numbers, purchase orders, time entry, vendor setup, payments, and other outstanding actions.
Preparation of recurring financial and operational reporting inputs for leadership and client reporting.
Escalation of financial and procurement risks to the Director of Operations and Project Management.
Onboarding, access, and business continuity
Coordination of onboarding and offboarding requirements for internal and external team members.
Management of access requests, distribution lists, org-level Slack channels, shared drives, YubiKeys, team rosters, and related documentation.
Identification and escalation of access, coverage, and continuity risks before they affect delivery.
Publishing and external-partner operations
Day-to-day operational coordination with Little Dot Studios and other operational partners.
Maintenance of partner access, documentation, escalation paths, actions, and outstanding dependencies.
Coordination with Account and Project Management to align publishing operations with client priorities and delivery plans.
Escalation of partner workflow and business-continuity concerns to the Director of Operations and Project Management.
Reporting and operational governance
Preparation of recurring operational reporting and tracking of monthly deliverables.
Monitoring of operational deadlines, required inputs, owners, and cross-functional follow-ups.
Documentation of decisions, owners, and next steps from key operational and financial forums.
Quality control of operational data and reporting before leadership or client distribution.

5+ years of progressive operational leadership in a creative agency setting.
Experience in leading projects involving AI technology and data analytics.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated expertise in conducting comprehensive assessments and providing actionable recommendations.
Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and collaborate with diverse stakeholders.
Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to inspire and guide teams toward achieving strategic goals.
